tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic two-event root recovery boundary. Event 1 is already durable; root is unprocessed; event 2 append was attempted but its acknowledgment is unavailable at crash. Only two repository-observable durable states are admitted: event2 absent, or event2 present exactly once.

deterministic_probe.event_identity_rule: Resume tests durable-ledger membership by stable event identity before any append.

case_event2_absent.resume_action: Membership finds event2 absent, so append event2 once; verify event2 durable; only then mark root processed.

case_event2_already_durable_ack_lost.resume_action: Membership finds event2 already durable, so suppress re-append; then mark root processed.

scope_guard: Positive evidence is limited to this two-event root, stable event-identity membership, atomic repository-visible durable states, and the single ambiguous event2-append acknowledgment boundary. It does not establish torn/corrupt writes, identity collision resistance, concurrent writers, nested frames, other event counts, arbitrary Unicode classes, hostile-size behavior, or Phase-1 closure.
exact_next_action: Next valid invocation: after fresh authority freeze, own-state reconstruction, and persisted/read-back preflight, test exactly one adjacent root-processed-write acknowledgment ambiguity with both event1 and event2 already durable. Admit only repository-observable processed=false versus processed=true states; verify resume never appends either event again and converges to processed=true. Do not test concurrent writers, torn writes, another event count, or another boundary in that invocation.
